sections.instructionBn: Read the passage and answer the following questions.
sections.stimulusMd:
**Water pollution**

Shihab and Kaniz are walking to school along the river. At one place, they stop to see something. Some people are bathing in the river. Some are washing their clothes. A man throws some rubbish into the river. Shihab and Kaniz become upset. They request the man, “Please, don’t throw the rubbish into the river. It pollutes the water.”

Shihab and Kaniz also see some polythene bags, plastic bottles and some other things floating on the river. They start talking about it.

Kaniz: Look, Shihab, the water is so dirty!
Shihab: Yes, Kaniz. We can’t bathe in this polluted water.
Kaniz: Fish also can’t swim easily.
Shihab: Yes. Sometimes, the fish gets caught into polythene bags. It puts them in danger.
Kaniz: You are right. We should save them.
Shihab: Sure. We must keep the water clean.

Kaniz and Shihab reach their school and share this story with their friends. They discuss how to keep the water clean and safe.

items.text: Where are Shihab and Kaniz walking?
items.answer: They are walking to school along the river.

items.text: What does the man throw into the river?
items.answer: He throws some rubbish into the river.

items.text: What things do they see floating on the river?
items.answer: They see polythene bags, plastic bottles and some other things floating on the river.

items.text: Why is the fish in danger?
items.answer: Sometimes the fish gets caught in polythene bags. It puts them in danger.

items.text: Who do Shihab and Kaniz share the story with?
items.answer: They share the story with their friends at school.

sections.instructionBn: Read the passage in question 1 again. Write True if the statement is correct. If the statement is false, write False and then give the correct answer.

items.answer: False. Shihab and Kaniz are walking to school.

items.text: Some people are washing their clothes in the river.
Shihab and Kaniz become happy when the man throws rubbish into the river.
items.answer: False. Shihab and Kaniz become upset.

items.text: Fish can swim easily in the dirty water.
items.answer: False. Fish can’t swim easily in the dirty water.
items.bookRef: EFT Unit 7, Lesson 1, activity D(e), p. 99

items.text: Write a dialogue about Islamic greetings and conversation with the shopkeeper for buying necessary things.
items.answer: Points to look for: opens with ‘Assalamu Alaikum’ and the reply ‘Wa Alaikumus Salam’; asks for the things needed (e.g. rice, pulses, soap, pencils); asks the price; shopkeeper gives the price; pays and takes the change; says ‘JazakAllahu khairan’ / thanks; closes with Salam. About 8–10 exchanges, correct names on each line, correct punctuation.

items.text: Write a paragraph about “The Importance of Water”.
items.answer: Points to look for: water is called life; humans, animals and plants need water to live; main sources — oceans, rivers, rain, ponds; we use water for drinking, cooking, bathing and cleaning; plants take water from the soil, farmers use water to grow crops; polluted water is dangerous, so we must not throw rubbish into water; we should save water (turn off the tap). About 8–10 sentences.

authorNotes: Scope: English for Today Units 4-8. The Mohammadpur Final 2026 seen passage (Nusair washing hands, Unit 6) is in the book but is NOT one of the four seen passages Sylhet published, so rows 1-2 use 'Water pollution' (Unit 7, Lesson 1), one of the listed passages, with new questions (no MP paper uses a listed passage). Row 1 and row 2 share that one passage; it is printed once in row 1. Reused from MP 2026 as-is: adjectives, pronouns (one story slip fixed: the father, not the mother, gave the prayer mat), adverbs, the 10 word meanings (they come from Unit 6, so they are in scope), the dialogue topic (shopkeeper) and the paragraph (Importance of Water). MP 2026's 'rewrite in Simple Present' and 'rearrange words' questions were not used because Sylhet has no such row. Noun & gender, articles, conjunctions and the other half of prepositions and punctuation came from MP Final 2025 and the Half-yearly papers; noun sentences were cut down to one noun each so each is worth exactly 1 mark. Right form of verbs: 3 Present Simple (MP 2025) + 2 Present Continuous (new, from the Ant and Grasshopper story), as the syllabus asks for both. Word meanings: answer key gives the Bangla meaning plus a simple English meaning — please tell teachers which one you expect. Two items accept two answers (cat 'under/on' the bed; 'and/but' in conjunction 3) — noted in the key. Duration '৩ ঘণ্টা' copied from the brief example; MP's paper is 2 hours 30 minutes — please confirm. Names in sentences (Omar, Bilal, Tarin, Rahim, Tanim, Asif, Rahat, Rafi) come from the MP papers or are generic — check none matches a Sylhet Class 3 child.
